skill.name: benchling-integration
skill.description: Guide Benchling integrations for registry entities, inventory, notebooks, workflows, events, authentication, and Data Warehouse analytics through the Python SDK and REST API.
skill.summary: Build secure Benchling data and laboratory workflow integrations with practical SDK and REST API guidance.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: All 143 static alerts are false positives caused by documentation examples, Markdown formatting, placeholders, and intended Benchling API access. No executable payloads, unrelated network destinations, real credentials, or prompt injection instructions were found. One high-severity semantic issue remains: verbose curl authentication tests can reveal authorization headers in terminal or CI logs.

remediation.issue: Verbose authentication tests can expose credentials in logs.
remediation.suggestion: Remove -v from authenticated examples, or require temporary credentials and immediate redaction of terminal and CI logs.

content.value_statement: Manual Benchling data operations slow laboratory teams and increase inconsistency. This skill guides secure API, SDK, registry, inventory, notebook, workflow, and analytics integrations.
actual_capabilities: Configure Benchling API key, OAuth client credential, or OIDC authentication patterns.
Create, read, update, list, register, and archive supported registry entities through the Python SDK.
Manage inventory containers, boxes, locations, transfers, and batch operations.
Create notebook entries, link entities, and automate workflow tasks with asynchronous task monitoring.
Use REST endpoint guidance for pagination, filtering, error handling, and custom requests.
Plan EventBridge integrations and Data Warehouse queries for downstream analytics and reporting.
limitations: Requires a Benchling tenant, valid credentials, and permissions for each requested operation.
Provides guidance and examples, but does not include executable scripts or a bundled Benchling client.
Tenant schemas, identifiers, app settings, and Data Warehouse access must be supplied by the user.
State-changing operations can affect regulated laboratory records and require independent review and approval.

use_cases.title: Synchronize research records
use_cases.description: Design registry and notebook integrations that move approved research metadata between Benchling and controlled external systems.

use_cases.title: Automate inventory operations
use_cases.description: Plan validated container, location, and transfer workflows with clear permission and approval checkpoints.

use_cases.title: Build event-driven applications
use_cases.description: Combine Benchling Apps, EventBridge events, workflow tasks, and reliable downstream processing.

prompt_templates.title: Connect securely
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to connect to my Benchling tenant with environment-based API key authentication. Include dependency setup, validation, and secret-handling precautions.

prompt_templates.title: Query registry entities
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a read-only Python SDK workflow that lists DNA sequences from folder [FOLDER_ID], handles pagination, and reports selected fields.

prompt_templates.title: Validate inventory transfers
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an inventory transfer for containers [IDS] into [DESTINATION_ID]. Include permission checks, dry-run validation, error handling, and approval before changes.

prompt_templates.title: Design an event integration
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced Benchling integration that routes [EVENT_TYPES] through EventBridge to [TARGET_SYSTEM]. Cover authentication, idempotency, retries, audit logging, and recovery.

output_examples.input: Prepare a safe plan to export DNA sequence metadata from folder FLD-123.
output: Scope: read-only DNA sequence listing limited to folder FLD-123.
Checks: verify tenant, permissions, requested fields, pagination, and expected record count.
Delivery: write approved metadata fields to a named destination after confirming overwrite behavior.

output_examples.input: Automate completion of eligible workflow tasks after validation.
output_examples.output: The workflow validates task status and required fields before any update. It records skipped tasks and requires approval before changing eligible tasks.

output_examples.input: Compare Benchling authentication methods for a new integration.
output: API keys suit personal scripts and prototypes.
OAuth client credentials suit service applications and controlled automation.
OIDC suits enterprise identity scenarios when the tenant supports it.

best_practices: Use least-privilege credentials, protected environment variables, and separate identities for development and production.
Begin with read-only queries and dry runs, then require explicit approval before creates, updates, transfers, archives, or workflow transitions.
Validate tenant identifiers, schemas, pagination, retries, and audit requirements before automating laboratory records.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys, client secrets, access tokens, or Data Warehouse credentials in prompts, source files, or logs.
Do not run bulk state changes without scoped filters, validation, backups, and an approval checkpoint.
Do not assume sample identifiers, schema fields, permissions, or tenant URLs match a production Benchling environment.

faq.question: What credentials are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers API keys, OAuth client credentials, and OIDC. Available methods depend on tenant configuration and the integration type.

faq.question: Does this skill connect automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation guidance and examples. Users must install dependencies, supply credentials, and authorize network or state-changing operations.

faq.question: Can it modify records?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented SDK patterns include create, update, transfer, archive, and workflow operations. Confirm permissions and obtain approval before execution.

faq.question: Does it support inventory and ELN?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers containers, boxes, transfers, notebook entries, entity links, and related workflow patterns.

faq.question: Can it query the Data Warehouse?
faq.answer: It explains access patterns and common analytics uses. Actual schemas, credentials, SQL clients, and query authorization remain tenant-specific.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use a secret manager or protected environment variables. Never include live secrets in prompts, source control, verbose logs, or shared output.
